---
title: "F&Q"
---

This page collects common setup and workflow questions.

## Installation and Startup

<details>
<summary><strong>I have downloaded the app, but it won't open.</strong></summary>

On macOS, this can happen because of security restrictions for apps
downloaded from the internet.

1. Open **System Settings**.
2. Go to **Privacy & Security**.
3. Find the blocked Neuralyzer app notice and click **Open Anyway**.
4. Launch Neuralyzer again.

For platform-specific installation steps, see
[Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).
</details>

## Data and Workflows

<details>
<summary><strong>Loading data</strong></summary>

Start with the [Data Loading Overview](user_guide/data_loading/index.qmd).

For video specifically, see [How to Import Video](examples/video_import.qmd).
Important warning: videos with B-frames are not supported for correct
frame-accurate behavior. See
[Checking for and Removing B-frames](examples/video_import.qmd#checking-for-and-removing-b-frames).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What are modules?</strong></summary>

Modules are major tools in Neuralyzer (for example Data Manager, Media
Viewer, Data Viewer, and Data Inspector). You can open them from the
main menus and use them together in one synchronized workspace.

See [Interacting with Your Data](concepts/interface_roles.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What are widgets?</strong></summary>

Widgets are dockable UI panels that make up the application. Each widget
focuses on a task (viewing media, editing labels, inspecting tables,
running transforms, etc.).

See [Interacting with Your Data](concepts/interface_roles.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>How do I play the video?</strong></summary>

Use the play button in the Media Viewer controls, or press the
spacebar to play/pause. If the shortcut does not trigger, click in the
media panel first to give it keyboard focus.

See [Media Viewer Overview](user_guide/media_viewer/overview.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What is a JSON file, and how do I write it?</strong></summary>

A JSON file is a structured text configuration that lets you define
repeatable loading workflows (media + features + clocks) so you can load
the same experiment setup quickly.

See [JSON Loading](user_guide/data_loading/JSON_loading.qmd) and
[Import via JSON Configuration](examples/video_import.qmd#json-import).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Will my data get deleted if I modify it in the program?</strong></summary>

Neuralyzer supports non-destructive workflows. Best practice is to keep
source keys separate from edited/derived keys and write transform output
to new keys.

See [Non-Destructive Workflows](concepts/no_write_access.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What is a mask?</strong></summary>

A mask is a binary region (a segmented shape) on an image/video frame.
Masks are used when full object shape matters, not just a single point.

See [Mask Loader](user_guide/data_loading/Mask_Loading.qmd) and
[Tutorial: Mask Labeling](learning-resources/tutorials/mask_labeling.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What is a line?</strong></summary>

A line is an ordered set of connected points with a base/reference end,
useful for structures like whiskers, contours, or centerlines.

See [Line Loader](user_guide/data_loading/Line_Loading.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What is RLE format?</strong></summary>

RLE means Run-Length Encoding: a compact way to store binary masks by
recording pixel runs instead of every pixel individually.

See [Mask CSV RLE (Developer Reference)](developer/DataManager/IO/mask_csv_rle.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>How can I save my data?</strong></summary>

Use Data Inspector export controls for the selected modality (for
example points, lines, intervals, analog, and tensors), typically to
CSV.

See [Interacting with Your Data](concepts/interface_roles.qmd) and
[CSV Plot Export](user_guide/export/csv_plot_export.qmd).
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What can I do with my data?</strong></summary>

Explore and derive new features with the Data Transform widget, where
you can convert data types, compute features, and build analysis
pipelines.

See [Transform Widget](user_guide/data_transformations/transforms_v2_widget.qmd)
for the full transform list and pipeline workflow.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>What if my modalities use different sampling rates or clocks?</strong></summary>

Use explicit TimeFrames and assign each feature to the correct time base.
Neuralyzer is designed to handle cross-modal synchronization across
TimeFrames.

See [TimeFrame](concepts/timeframe.qmd).
</details>
